entries.text: Signature Llama is the baseline AI at the heart of this site — a tiny language model written and trained from scratch by Justin Addam Higgins. About 3 million parameters, a decoder-only transformer with a character-level tokenizer, trained on the IWB Dictionary and Signature spec text. It runs 100% in the browser in pure JavaScript, currently free for all internet tasks, no API keys. An independent model, not affiliated with Meta.
entries.title: What is Signature Llama?

entries.text: From absolute scratch, in four stages: 1) the corpus builder gathered the IWB Dictionary definitions and spec text into one training file; 2) the tokenizer learned a character-level vocabulary; 3) the trainer ran a small transformer on it with PyTorch until the loss settled; 4) the exporter quantized the weights to int8 and packed them for the browser engine. Every line of model code was hand-written — no borrowed architecture code, no pretrained weights.
entries.title: How was it built?

entries.text: Copy the 3-line embed code from the Use-it section: include sigllama.js, call SigLlama.load() with the model folder URL, then SigLlama.generate() with your prompt. That is the whole integration — no keys, no server, no build step.
entries.title: How do I use it in my project?

entries.text: Check the pill at the top of this page: it reads NOW TRAINING until the weights publish, then flips to LIVE by itself. The chat, downloads, and one-click patch all switch on automatically the moment it lands.
entries.title: Is the trained model live yet?

entries.text: No. Signature Llama is an independent model created by Justin Addam Higgins, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Meta Platforms or the LLaMA model family. The name is branding for the Signature line of AI.
entries.title: Is it related to Meta's Llama?

entries.text: Version 1 is about 3 million parameters — tiny by industry standards, which is the point: it downloads in seconds and runs on a phone. Small, lively, a little quirky — and it gets retrained on new words and specs so it keeps growing smarter.
entries.title: How big is it?

entries.text: The IWB Dictionary's original definitions plus the Signature spec archive. Nothing scraped, nothing borrowed — the model only knows the text it was trained on.
entries.title: What was it trained on?

entries.text: The pure-JavaScript inference engine. It loads the weights and vocabulary, runs the transformer math in your browser, and exposes SigLlama.load(), SigLlama.generate(), SigLlama.loaded(), and SigLlama.info(). No dependencies — one script tag and it works.
entries.title: sigllama.js — what is it?

entries.text: The trained model's brain: all ~3 million parameters, quantized to int8 so the file is just a few megabytes. The engine reads it at load time. This is the file that appears when training finishes.
entries.title: sigllama-v1.bin — what is it?

entries.text: The character-to-ID map the tokenizer learned. The engine uses it to turn your text into token IDs and turn the model's output IDs back into readable text.
entries.title: vocab.json — what is it?

entries.text: The Python script that learned the character-level vocabulary from the corpus and saved vocab.json. It also verifies the tokenizer round-trips text perfectly.
entries.title: tokenizer.py — what is it?

entries.text: The transformer itself, hand-written in PyTorch: embeddings, rotary positions, multi-head attention, feed-forward layers, and the output head. About a hundred lines — the whole brain, readable in one sitting.
entries.title: model.py — what is it?

entries.text: The training script: loads the corpus, runs the forward and backward passes with the AdamW optimizer, follows a cosine learning-rate schedule, saves checkpoints, and stops at the best validation loss.
entries.title: train.py — what is it?

entries.text: The exporter and quantizer: takes the best checkpoint, squeezes every weight matrix to int8 with per-row scales, and packs weights plus vocabulary into the compact sigllama-v1.bin the browser engine reads.
entries.title: export.py — what is it?

entries.text: The corpus builder: gathers the IWB Dictionary definitions and Signature spec texts into one clean training file, ready for the tokenizer and trainer.
entries.title: build_corpus.py — what is it?

entries.text: The open-source machine learning library used to train Signature Llama. It handles tensors, automatic gradients, and GPU math — the trainer is written against it.
entries.title: PyTorch — what is it?

entries.text: Python's number-crunching library for fast array math. Used in the data preparation and export steps around training.
entries.title: NumPy — what is it?

entries.text: The neural network design behind modern language models: stacked blocks of attention plus feed-forward networks. Signature Llama implements it from scratch in model.py rather than importing it.
entries.title: The transformer architecture

entries.text: The tool that actually teaches the model: it shows the transformer billions of characters, measures how wrong its predictions are, and nudges every parameter to do better — thousands of small steps until the loss settles.
entries.title: The trainer (tool)

entries.text: The tool that converts a trained PyTorch checkpoint into the compact binary the browser engine loads — quantization and packing included.
entries.title: The exporter (tool)

entries.text: The tool that shrinks the model: it converts 32-bit weights to 8-bit integers with per-row scales, cutting the file to a quarter of its size with barely any quality loss.
entries.title: The quantizer (tool)

entries.text: The tool that runs the trained model: sigllama.js loads the weights and generates text token by token, entirely in the browser.
entries.title: The inference engine (tool)

entries.text: The part of generation that picks each next token: temperature controls how adventurous the picks are, and top-k limits choices to the k most likely tokens. Both are options on SigLlama.generate().
entries.title: The sampler (temperature / top-k)

entries.text: Lists of numbers that capture what each token means — learned during training so similar characters and words get similar numbers. They are the model's first step in understanding text.
entries.title: Embeddings

entries.text: The talk box on this page: it keeps your conversation history, sends it to the model with each message, and streams the reply back. The code seam is LlamaChat.send(text).
entries.title: The chat UI

entries.text: The honest facts panel at the top of this page: size, architecture, training data, and the v1 honesty note. Developers can read the same facts live via SigLlama.info().
entries.title: The model card

The Tool Library
entries.text: The Tool Library is a wing of this site with 120+ plug-in tool libraries — real, runnable JavaScript for text, thinking, memory, chat, search, math, web, data, voice, safety, embedding and fun. Each library registers under SigLlama.tools.<id>, and every one ships with copy-code, download-.js, a network snippet to load it on your own sites, and a deep link like ?toollib=text-shorten. At the top sits the OPTIMAL ALL-PURPOSE SETTING: the recommended default setup (temperature 0.7, topK 40, maxTokens 120, plus the essential libraries) with a one-click 'Apply optimal settings' button. The card builds itself from the library index, so every new library flagged optimal joins automatically.
